title.dek: Jev vs GPT-6 Luna vs plain code, across three small tests. Every number on screen comes from saved API responses.
title.fine: Personal experiment, 6–7 Oct 2026. Jev 1.13.0 via the author's TypeSafe credits; GPT-6 Luna via the OpenAI API. Small authored tests, not benchmarks.

navres.title: Reasoning made Luna a planner. The BFS code already was one.
navres.fine: 12 authored 7×7 worlds (4 families × 3 rotations), one run each. Latency: median client time per move. Cost: recorded tokens × published list price, an estimate, not an invoice.

text.hybrid_fine: Notes hand-written after the keyword rules were frozen. Answers come from a stated policy applied to hidden attributes. Verdicts are the saved responses to these exact notes; robot motion is illustrative.
text.results_title: Short bounded calls: Jev. Planning: reasoning, or code.
text.results_fine: Banking77 subset of 12 confusable intents. Gate rule fixed before test: highest coverage with ≤5% dev error and ≥30 accepted. Luna confidence is self-reported; Jev's comes from its returned probabilities.
text.foot_routing: Most Luna misses were “needs review” (35 none, 51 reasoning, vs 7 Jev). Committed answers were ~96% correct for all three.
text.foot_gate: No Luna threshold met the dev rule; both missed at 0.95 (6.0% error without reasoning, 5.3% with). Jev's 0.8 gate: 202 automated, 2 wrong.
text.foot_messy: Safety misses (danger automated): rules 7, every model 0. Luna's misses were over-escalations; Jev's were wait-vs-reroute near-ties.

lines: Test the confidence before you gate on it.
end.fine: Methods, prompts, raw responses and rerun scripts accompany the write-up. OpenAI's Decisions API returned 403 for this key and was not tested.
